answer: The grader can be cheated, and it misjudges work.

In real episodes, Attackers reproduced hack-1 (grader_tampering, check-0003) with the full hint (0007-attacker, reward 1): "planted a bash shim that prints the pass marker"; had valid work rejected while testing hack-2 (unchecked_requirements, check-0004) with the full hint (0008-attacker, reward 0): "wrote the answer with leading zeros"; cheated while testing hack-1 (grader_tampering, check-0003) with the minimal hint, not confirmed as that finding (0014-attacker, reward 1): "wrote the pass marker without running the tests".
In copies of the task package, the hack inspector evidenced cheats by grader_tampering (check-0003, check-0008), timing_interference (check-0009); and valid work rejected (check-0004).
4 problems from 4 hack inspector findings and 1 grader inspector finding; the attack selects one candidate for each.
In copies of the task package, the grader inspector evidenced invalid work accepted (check-0000); and valid work rejected (check-0001).
The run is complete: simulation complete, grader complete, hack complete, attack complete.

notes: xiaomi_mimo/mimo-v2.6-pro reward: mixed, from 0.0 to 1.0; descriptive only; difficulty, sampling and execution conditions limit what rewards show
Local over-credit and under-credit labels compare one native reward with one deserved score. They are not binary FP/FN labels, and legitimate partial credit is not a false pass.

F1, AUROC and the false discovery and false negative rates compare native decisions and scores with evidence-grounded grader inspector references. nudi checks their retained provenance and consistency, not semantic correctness or calibrated accuracy. Whether a reference's requirements match the grader's acceptance rule is the grader inspector's interpretation, not independently validated.

Grader agreement covers binary rewards only. False discovery rate is FP / (TP + FP) and false negative rate is FN / (TP + FN); both are observed proportions of the eligible episodes, not multiple-testing guarantees, and the false positive rate FP / (FP + TN) is a different quantity. The default 12 ordinary runs give rough estimates. Unresolved episodes may be systematically harder, so the rates describe the eligible subset, not the whole pool. A presumed label stands in for the grader's own verdict, so rates that use one are lower bounds and F1 is then an upper bound.

Each candidate, hint level, and no-hint discovery stops at its first independently evidenced exploit, so attempt counts give no unbiased success-rate estimate. Not found means not found within the actual attempts. Only the attack inspector's attribution to a check of the same episode confirms the candidate under test; an unrelated or unattributed exploit does not.

An evidenced finding is accepted_invalid (violating work received more than its deserved score) or rejected_valid (valid work received less than it deserved). A finding with open conditions is still evidenced; its open conditions are listed beside it. A legitimate finding has a reward equal to its deserved score and no open condition, which does not judge the work. An inconclusive finding established no outcome, or is legitimate with an open condition. Package findings come from an Inspector sandbox running a copy of the task package, native findings from a task episode. An earlier reading of a check stays listed, marked with the later reading that superseded it. Category settlement and the evidenced count read the latest reading of each check; local labels and metrics read every reading.

A category is evidenced_issue once one of its cases is evidenced (for the hack inspector, an accepted_invalid case), and a later reading does not withdraw it. It is no_evidenced_issue only when a focused attempt completed it after any failure on it, none of its probes was skipped or repeated, its applicability evidence is applicable, at least one case measured in it before the episode sessions has a consistent latest reading, and the latest reading of every such case is consistent with its reward or evidenced; otherwise it stays unknown. A positive reward on a reading with any violated requirement is not consistent, even as correct partial credit. With no focused attempts, no category is no_evidenced_issue. A case belongs to the category of its experiment. A hack inspector case outside the requested categories keeps its own family, or `other` when none fits, and leaves the requested categories alone; an open grader inspector case without an inspected category keeps every category open. A repair, which interprets an ordinary check again in a later session, evidences the category of that session. The Inspector's applicability text is in the JSON report.

flags.text: 2 of 12 usable 'reward' rewards are below the rest by the quartile rule (0004-simulator 0, 0005-simulator 0; median 1, lower fence 1). None recorded an error, timeout or refusal. A few lower rewards in a mostly higher pool can come from model mistakes, sampling, time limits, refusals or infrastructure failures, or from the tail of an ordinary spread. They can also come from a grader that rejects valid work or a prompt that admits another reading. This is a reward pattern, not a finding; reading these episodes beside higher ones is the next step. 10 of 12 are 1 (95% Wilson interval 0.55 to 0.95 for its share, assuming independent episodes); SD and skewness follow from this share. Every named episode has a presumed or unsupported label, so grader inspection did not examine this pattern.
